summary.intent: Unlock TurboQuant KV cache compression on a Framework Desktop with Strix Halo iGPU (gfx1151), starting from a post-BIOS-change state where VRAM was increased from 0.5 GB to 64 GB.
summary.outcome: Discovered that extensive prior work already exists (0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 installed, architectural wiring complete, session-94 documented the real blocker), but TurboQuant is not yet running on the iGPU due to a PyTorch ROCm wheel ISA gap for gfx1151. A Triton kernel smoke test was proposed as the decisive next step but not yet executed.

repo: research/turboquant/ contains 0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 with real Triton kernels + vLLM attention backend, installed as egg in cohezion/.venv — the actual TurboQuant implementation, not just schema/oracle code
cohezion/.venv has vLLM 0.19.0 installed but it is broken: torch 2.5.1+rocm6.2 lacks torch._inductor.custom_graph_pass that vLLM 0.19.0 requires
The turboquant integration is NOT a --kv-cache-dtype CLI flag; it is a Python vLLM attention backend plugin registered via VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND or similar
turboquant_axis dict is injected into every inference payload; cache-gateway unlock sets TRITON_AMD_WMMA=1 + HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.1

Session 94 (2026-04-16) established the real blocker: PyTorch ROCm wheels lack valid ISA for gfx1151 — HSA_OVERRIDE does not fix this, it is an upstream wheel issue causing Invalid Device Function / Memory access fault on first Triton dispatch
local_environment_quirks.md contains distilled session-94 findings that supersede the original plan's assumptions — must be read before planning hardware upgrade steps
Fleet lane :13306 is the only live lane with a loaded model (DeepSeek-R1-Qwen3-8B via Lemonade/NPU); ports :13307/:13308/:13309 are placeholder daemons with nothing on GPU
llama.cpp master is pre-built at ~/src/llama.cpp/build/bin/ with HIP support, hipcc 7.2.53211 available, but on master branch — no TurboQuant PR pulled
rocm-smi reports full 64 GB VRAM; the 31 GB figure seen via HSA is a per-process allocation ceiling, not a hardware cap — GTT exposes 128 GB for spillover
launch_fleet_safe.sh uses Lemonade as llama.cpp orchestrator with tested flags (-fa 1 -ngl 99, HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.1) — use this instead of raw llama-server invocations

code.finding: Returns silently (return) when GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD credential is missing — silent-failure anti-pattern; should raise SystemExit(2) for non-zero propagation through CI/cron/loop drivers

Newly created consolidated send script (90 lines): reads --subject and --body-file, markdown->HTML via markdown2 if present, raises EmailNotConfigured with remediation text on missing credential, uses smtplib.SMTP_SSL(smtp.gmail.com, 465) pattern

0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 — complete Triton kernels + vLLM backend integration. CUDA-tested only, no ROCm/gfx1151/HIP markers. Key kernel: fused_rotate_quantize_kernel. Benchmarked on RTX 5090: 2x context extension, 30-77% KV savings, 3-bit cos_sim 1.000000
178-line PyTorch oracle for correctness gating — separate from 0xSero kernels, used to verify TurboQuant dispatch output matches paper tolerances

Contains distilled session-94 TurboQuant findings including the PyTorch ROCm wheel ISA gap for gfx1151, correct HSA_OVERRIDE value (11.5.1 not 11.5.0), and recommended workarounds (NPU/FLM path, direct llama.cpp HIP)

workflow: Gmail MCP create_draft sidesteps GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD entirely — drafts land in Gmail for human review/send; cleaner than smtplib for interactive sessions, smtplib is still correct for automated pipelines
llama.cpp -fit on (default) hangs at 99% CPU for 2+ minutes on large GGUF models on this host; always pass -fit off to avoid the auto-fit hang
Check SESSION_HANDOFF_*.md and HANDOFF_*.md files at session start before planning work — prior sessions leave substantial artifacts that avoid duplicate effort
kernel.ubuntu.com mainline v6.18.4 build failed (empty directory); v6.18.23 is the current 6.18 longterm release (built 2026-04-18). Always verify kernel version existence before planning installs
The cappelikan/ppa mainline GUI tool adds a persistent apt source — requires explicit user consent beyond just 'upgrade kernel'; direct .deb from kernel.ubuntu.com is the auditable alternative

Bitwarden CLI on this host points to a self-hosted server (mike-poweredge-t30.tail54eb71.ts.net:8222) that may be unreachable from the dev machine; vault is also locked — do not depend on bw for credential retrieval in automated flows
rocm-smi vs HSA allocation discrepancy: rocm-smi reports full VRAM (64 GB), HSA per-process ceiling shows ~31 GB — normal for UMA APUs, GTT handles spillover
The kernel/firmware/ROCm upgrade path is orthogonal to TurboQuant — it addresses VRAM headroom and driver stability but adds zero TurboQuant code; do not conflate the two upgrade goals

friction: Plan cited llama.cpp PR #20969 as the TurboQuant implementation — it is actually a discussion thread, not a PR; caused significant planning misdirection
vLLM 0.19.0 in cohezion/.venv is broken due to torch 2.5.1+rocm6.2 vs vLLM's torch 2.6+ API requirement — ImportError on first use
llama.cpp auto-fit algorithm hung at 99% CPU single-threaded for 2+ minutes; no progress indicator, appeared frozen — required kill and -fit off workaround
TURBOQUANT_UNLOCK_REPORT.md from session 94 was deleted from disk; its findings were only recoverable via local_environment_quirks.md — lost primary source
EmailNotifier class is imported by 5+ scripts but has no class definition anywhere in tracked code — orphaned import pattern causes silent failures at runtime
11 near-identical send_*.py scripts across the project — each sprint created a new variant instead of a shared utility
Bitwarden self-hosted server unreachable from dev machine, vault locked — credential retrieval path blocked during email verification step
rocm-smi showed 64 GB VRAM but llama.cpp HSA reported 31 GB — required investigation to distinguish hardware cap from per-process allocation limit
BIOS on this Framework Desktop does not expose AI Max Performance or PCIe Gen5 options — likely requires BIOS firmware update (v3.05+), not accessible via OS
